subject: Proposal: measurement-bucket consolidation + temporary bridging plan for p50/p95 hosted API SLOs
messages:
From: Jake Park <jake.park@finnova.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai
Date: Sun, 22 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Challenge with p95 measurement buckets and monthly SLO for hosted API

Hi Rachel,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked Redwood's latency profiles and the cost controls. One operational concern came up during our SRE review: the way p95 is being measured across short rolling buckets exposes us to monthly credit risk because a handful of isolation events in an unlucky hour can push the monthly p95 over the commitment.

Specifically: FinNova's traffic is spiky (batch imports + interactive widgets). We saw three minutes last week where a regional infra issue inflated the p95 for that 1-hour bucket and caused our monitoring to flag a breach even though the rest of the month looked fine. For a contracted monthly p95 that matters.

Can Redwood propose either:
- a measurement consolidation (e.g., aggregate p95 across overlapping buckets / longer windows), or
- a formal temporary exception / bridging plan while we onboard a dedicated caching layer that reduces tail latency?

We need something that reduces the likelihood of a single short blip causing a contract-level credit. Curious what the typical redress you offer for hosted customers in this situation is and whether we can get a short one-off addendum while we complete our integration work.

Attach: sample p95 report (CSV) and a short timeline for our cache rollout.

Thanks,
Jake Park
SRE Lead, FinNova

Attachments referenced: finnova-p95-sample-20260320.csv
From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jake Park <jake.park@finnova.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Mar 2026 11:38:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Challenge with p95 measurement buckets and monthly SLO for hosted API

Hi Jake — appreciate the clear reproduction and the sample report.

Short answer: yes, we can do a pragmatic, time-boxed bridging plan while you finish the caching rollout. I sketched two complementary approaches below and attached a draft SLO addendum and a diagram of the measurement buckets for reference.

Option A — Measurement-bucket consolidation (preferred):
- For your account we aggregate p95 across rolling 6-hour windows (instead of strict 1-hour buckets) for the purpose of monthly SLO computation.
- This reduces sensitivity to short, concentrated blips while preserving visibility into tail behavior.
- Retroactive application: we can start the consolidated measurement at the beginning of the next billing period.

Option B — Temporary bridging exception:
- 60-day exception where a single 1-hour bucket exceeding threshold will not automatically trigger a month-level credit if the 6-hour consolidated p95 remains within target.
- During the exception period Redwood Support and FinNova SRE will run a joint post-mortem for any qualifying hour > threshold.

Operational controls and safeguards:
- We will enable enhanced tracing for your routes and provide a token-level breakdown for any flagged period.
- Automatic alerts and a playbook will be applied to triage events that would otherwise look like a breach.
- If an event appears to be caused by customer-side changes (large bursts from your side), exceptions may be denied; otherwise Redwood will apply the bridging rule.

Next steps: if you prefer Option A we can prepare a short addendum and change the measurement window for billing. If you prefer Option B we can issue a 60-day bridging addendum and set a review checkpoint at day 30.

I've looped in Monica and Karthik to coordinate legal/finance wording and telemetry gating. Attached: slo-addendum-draft-20260330.pdf (redline) and measurement-buckets-diagram.png.

Would you like us to prepare a DocuSign-ready addendum for Option A (measurement consolidation) or Option B (temporary bridging)?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Attachments: slo-addendum-draft-20260330.pdf
From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Proposal: measurement-bucket consolidation + temporary bridging plan for p50/p95 hosted API SLOs

Rachel / Karthik — quick internal on the options. Quoting Rachel's summary below for context.

On Option A (6-hour consolidated measurement):
- Legal: easier to operationalize; minimal redlines. Need a clear definition of how rolling windows align with billing cycles (we recommend "align to UTC day with 6-hour rolling aggregation for billing computation").
- Finance: OK with retroactive start at next billing period; ensure we cap retroactive liability.

On Option B (60-day bridging):
- Legal: accept but want explicit criteria for denial (e.g., deliberate customer-induced spikes) and an audit trail obligation.
- Product/Telemetry: provide the link to the internal SLO visualization (we should share a scoped view with FinNova). Also recommend an automated replay checklist for incidents that qualify for an exception.

Recommendation: Offer Option A as the default but include Option B as an immediate, one-off short-lived fallback if FinNova prefers no delay. Draft language suggestions are in the attached PDF.

If we proceed with Option A, I will:
- finalize legal wording for the addendum,
- confirm billing start date coordination with Finance,
- schedule a 30-day check-in with the customer success lead.

Please advise if you'd like me to send the DocuSign package or hand it off to AE to send.

--
Monica Patel
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
From: Jake Park <jake.park@finnova.com>
To: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
Cc: FinNova SRE Team <sre@finnova.com>
Date: Mon, 30 Mar 2026 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: measurement-bucket consolidation + temporary bridging plan for p50/p95 hosted API SLOs

Rachel / Monica — thanks for the fast turnaround. After an internal readout we prefer Option A (measurement-bucket consolidation to a 6-hour rolling aggregation) to reduce noise in monthly billing and avoid administrative exceptions. Option B is fine as a fallback but not necessary if Option A is applied at the next billing cycle.

Please proceed with the addendum for Option A and share the DocuSign link. We'll expect the consolidated measurement to begin on 2026-04-01 and would like the scoped telemetry view you mentioned so our SREs can validate once the new window is live.

Also request a joint 30-day check-in with Redwood CS/AE to review observed tail behavior and confirm whether a permanent change is warranted.

Thanks,
Jake Park
SRE Lead, FinNova

Forwarded attachments requested: slo-addendum-draft-20260330.pdf
DocuSign preference: Jake will route to procurement and legal internally once provided.
